claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC, dendritic alloy.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding less than approximately 5 at.% Hf and applying a controlled aging treatment will induce nanoscale Hf-rich precipitates.
The induced precipitates will be Hf-rich carbides or intermetallics.
The induced precipitates will be thermally stable and homogeneously dispersed in the BCC matrix.
Nanoscale Hf-rich precipitates will impede dislocation glide.
Nanoscale Hf-rich precipitates will suppress dynamic recovery at 1273 K.
Impeded dislocation motion and suppressed dynamic recovery will increase high-temperature yield and compressive strengths relative to unmodified TiVNbTa.
The modified alloy may exceed 500 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
The modified alloy may maintain ductility to approximately 30% strain at 1273 K.
Keeping the Hf addition below approximately 5 at.% will preserve the single-phase BCC structure while promoting precipitation.
The proposed precipitates may coarsen if the heat treatment is not properly controlled.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on optimization of precipitate volume fraction, size, and stability.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the modified alloy should preserve a single-phase BCC structure, whereas the intervention and mediator require formation of carbide or intermetallic precipitates, which would make the microstructure multiphase.
